english_meaning: By One More Than the Previous One

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, how can we calculate 35 × 35 quickly without performing long multiplication?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, how can we calculate 35 times 35 quickly without performing long multiplication?</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Long multiplication? Not in our Gurukul! With Ekādhikena Pūrveṇa — 'By One More Than the Previous One' — we do it in seconds! Take the part before the final 5, multiply it by one more than itself, and place 25 at the end.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Long multiplication? Not in our Gurukul! With Ekadhikena Purvena — By One More Than the Previous One — we do it in seconds! Take the part before the final five, multiply it by one more than itself, and place 25 at the end.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Watch! For 35²: the part before 5 is 3. One more than 3 is 4. Multiply: 3 × 4 = 12. Place 25 after it — and you have 1225!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Watch! For 35 squared: the part before 5 is 3. One more than 3 is 4. Multiply: 3 times 4 equals 12. Place 25 after it — and you have 1225!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Your turn, Shishya! For 45², apply the sutra to the prefix: what is 4 × (4 + 1)?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Your turn, Shishya! For 45 squared, apply the sutra to the prefix: what is 4 times open-parenthesis 4 plus 1 close-parenthesis?</speak>

english_meaning: All from 9 and the Last from 10

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, subtracting 1000 - 364 by borrowing across zeros is slow and confusing!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Guru-ji, subtracting 1000 minus 364 by borrowing across zeros is slow and confusing!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Instead of tedious borrowing across zeros, use Nikhilam: All from 9, and the Last from 10.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Instead of tedious borrowing across zeros, use Nikhilam: All from 9, and the Last from 10.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Observe: 9 - 3 = 6, 9 - 6 = 3, and the last digit 10 - 4 = 6. Put them together: 636!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Observe: 9 minus 3 is 6, 9 minus 6 is 3, and the last digit 10 minus 4 is 6. Put them together: 636!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Your turn, Shishya! For 1000 - 427: all from 9 gives 5 and 7. What is 10 - 7 for the last digit?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Your turn, Shishya! For 1000 minus 427: all from 9 gives 5 and 7. What is 10 minus 7 for the last digit?</speak>

interactive_handshake.prompt_text: What is 10 - 7? Enter the final digit.

english_meaning: By One Less Than the Previous One

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, how can we calculate 47 × 99 quickly without performing long multiplication?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, how can we calculate 47 times 99 quickly without performing long multiplication?</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: When multiplying by nines, invoke Ekanyūnena Pūrveṇa — 'By One Less than the Previous One'! Lessen the multiplicand by 1 for the left part, then subtract that from the nines for the right part.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>When multiplying by nines, invoke Ekanyunena Purvena — By One Less than the Previous One! Lessen the multiplicand by 1 for the left part, then subtract that from the nines for the right part.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Watch closely! For 47 × 99: lessen 47 by 1 to get 46 on the left. Then subtract from nines: 99 − 46 gives 53 on the right. Put them together: 4653!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Watch closely! For 47 times 99: lessen 47 by 1 to get 46 on the left. Then 99 minus 46 gives 53 on the right. Put them together: 4653!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Your turn, Shishya! For 53 × 99, apply Ekanyunena to the multiplicand: what is 53 − 1?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Your turn, Shishya! For 53 times 99, apply Ekanyunena to the multiplicand: what is 53 minus 1?</speak>

interactive_handshake.prompt_text: What is 53 − 1? Enter the left part.

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, calculating 94² in my head sounds daunting without multiplying 94 × 94 on paper!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, how can we calculate 94 squared in our head without long multiplication?</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Near a base like 100, invoke Yāvadūnam — 'By the Deficiency'! Lessen the number by its deficiency from 100 for the left part, then square the deficiency for the right part.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Near a base like 100, invoke Yavadunam — By the Deficiency! Lessen the number by its deficiency for the left part, then square the deficiency for the right part.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Observe: 94 is 6 below 100. Lessen 94 by 6 to get 88 on the left. Then square the deficiency: 6² = 36 on the right. Put them together: 8836!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Observe: 94 is 6 below 100. Lessen 94 by 6 to get 88 on the left. Then square 6 to get 36 on the right. Put them together: 8836!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Your turn, Shishya! For 97², the deficiency from 100 is 3. Apply Yāvadūnam to find the left part: what is 97 − 3?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Your turn, Shishya! For 97 squared, the deficiency from 100 is 3. What is 97 minus 3 for the left part?</speak>

interactive_handshake.prompt_text: What is 97 − 3? Enter the left part.

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, how can we multiply arbitrary numbers like 23 × 41 without a long multiplication grid?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, how can we multiply arbitrary numbers like 23 times 41 without a long multiplication grid?</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Welcome to the universal key! Invoke Ūrdhva-Tiryagbhyām — 'Vertically and Crosswise'! We cast three rays: right vertical for units, crosswise sum for tens, and left vertical for hundreds.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Welcome to the universal key! Invoke Urdhva-Tiryagbhyam — Vertically and Crosswise! Three simple rays give the entire product in a single line.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Watch: right vertical is 3 × 1 = 3. Crosswise is (2 × 1) + (3 × 4) = 14: write 4, carry 1. Left vertical is (2 × 4) + 1 = 9. Combine them: 943!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Watch: right vertical is 3 times 1 equals 3. Crosswise is 2 plus 12 equals 14: write 4, carry 1. Left vertical is 8 plus 1 equals 9. Combine them: 943!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Your turn, Shishya! For 31 × 21, apply the crosswise step: what is (3 × 1) + (1 × 2) for the middle digit?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Your turn, Shishya! For 31 times 21, apply the crosswise step: what is 3 times 1 plus 1 times 2?</speak>

interactive_handshake.prompt_text: What is (3 × 1) + (1 × 2)? Enter the middle digit.

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, dividing numbers like 1225 ÷ 12 always forces me into tedious long division with guesses and subtractions!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, dividing numbers like 1225 by 12 always forces me into tedious long division!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Transform division into simple addition! Invoke Parāvartya Yojayet — 'Transpose and Apply'! For divisor 12 near base 10, transpose deviation +2 into −2. Multiply each quotient digit by −2 and add across columns!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Transform division into addition! Invoke Paravartya Yojayet — Transpose and Apply! Transpose plus 2 into minus 2, then multiply and add across columns.</prosody></speak>
<speak>Watch 1225 divided by 12: drop 1, add down to get 0, then 2. The remainder is 5 plus minus 4, which is 1! Quotient is 102, remainder 1!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Your turn, Shishya! For 144 ÷ 12, drop 1 as the first quotient digit. What is the next quotient digit: 4 + (1 × −2)?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Your turn, Shishya! For 144 divided by 12, drop 1 as the first quotient digit. What is 4 plus 1 times minus 2?</speak>

english_meaning: If One is in Ratio, the Other is Zero

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, solving systems like 3x + 2y = 12 and 6x + 5y = 24 with elimination takes so many algebraic steps!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, solving simultaneous equations with elimination takes so many algebraic steps!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Spot the symmetry! Invoke Ānurūpye Śūnyamanyat — 'If One is in Ratio, the Other is Zero'! If the ratio of x-coefficients matches the constant ratio, the other variable y vanishes to zero!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Spot the symmetry! Invoke Anurupye Shunyamanyat — If One is in Ratio, the Other is Zero! When the x-ratio matches the constant ratio, y vanishes directly to zero.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Look closely: 3/6 = 12/24 = 1/2, so y = 0 immediately! Substitute y = 0 into 3x + 2(0) = 12: 3x = 12, so x = 4! The solution is x = 4, y = 0 without any elimination!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Look closely: 3 over 6 equals 12 over 24, so y is zero immediately! Then 3x equals 12, giving x equals 4 in one step!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now your turn, Shishya! In 2x + 3y = 8 and 4x + 7y = 16, the x-ratio (2/4) matches the constants (8/16), so y = 0. Solve for x: 2x = 8.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now your turn, Shishya! The x-ratio matches the constants, so y is zero. Solve for x: 2x equals 8!</speak>

interactive_handshake.prompt_text: Solve for x: 2x = 8. Tap the value of x.

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, for 45x - 23y = 113 and 23x - 45y = 91, the numbers are huge! Cross-multiplying by 45 and 23 will take pages of messy algebra!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, for 45x minus 23y equals 113 and 23x minus 45y equals 91, the numbers are huge! Cross-multiplying will take pages of messy algebra!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Observe the cross-symmetry: the coefficients 45 and -23 interchange! Invoke Saṅkalana-Vyavakalanābhyām — 'By Addition and by Subtraction'! Simply add the equations once, and subtract them once, to reduce them to simple mental arithmetic!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Observe the cross-symmetry! The coefficients interchange. Invoke Sankalana-Vyavakalanabhyam — By Addition and by Subtraction! Simply add the equations once, and subtract them once, to reduce them to simple mental arithmetic.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Step 1 (Addition): Adding both equations gives 68x - 68y = 204. Divide by 68 to get x - y = 3! Step 2 (Subtraction): Subtracting Eq 2 from Eq 1 gives 22x + 22y = 22. Divide by 22 to get x + y = 1!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Step 1: Adding gives 68x minus 68y equals 204, so x minus y is 3! Step 2: Subtracting gives 22x plus 22y equals 22, so x plus y is 1!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now verify the subtraction step, Shishya! From 22x + 22y = 22, dividing both sides by 22 gives x + y. What is 22 ÷ 22?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now verify the subtraction step, Shishya! Dividing 22x plus 22y equals 22 by 22 gives x plus y. What is 22 divided by 22?</speak>

english_meaning: When the Collection is the Same, it is Zero

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji, expanding 7(x + 1) = 8(x + 1) gives 7x + 7 = 8x + 8. Moving terms across the equals sign feels tedious when both sides share the exact same factor (x + 1)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody pitch='+2st'>Guru-ji, expanding 7 times x plus 1 equals 8 times x plus 1 feels tedious when both sides share the exact same factor!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Spot the common factor! Invoke Śūnyaṁ Sāmyasamuccaye — 'When the Collection is the Same, it is Zero'! When a shared factor appears on both sides with unequal multipliers, that common expression must vanish to zero!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Spot the common factor! Invoke Shunyam Samyasamuccaye — When the Collection is the Same, it is Zero! When a shared factor appears on both sides with unequal multipliers, that common expression must vanish to zero.</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Subtract both sides: (7 - 8)(x + 1) = 0, giving -1(x + 1) = 0! Since -1 cannot be zero, the common factor must be zero: x + 1 = 0! Subtracting 1 yields x = -1 instantly, without expanding any brackets!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Subtracting both sides gives minus 1 times x plus 1 equals 0. Since minus 1 cannot be zero, x plus 1 must be zero, giving x equals minus 1 instantly!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now test your understanding, Shishya! In 7(x + 1) = 8(x + 1), since 7 ≠ 8, the common factor must equal zero: x + 1 = 0. Solve for x!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now test your understanding, Shishya! Since 7 does not equal 8, the common factor must equal zero: x plus 1 equals 0. Solve for x!</speak>

interactive_handshake.prompt_text: Solve for x: x + 1 = 0. Tap the value of x.

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Guru-ji! In x² + 6x + 8 = 0, trial-and-error factoring is slow when numbers get large. How does Vedic math solve quadratics directly?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Guru-ji! In x squared plus 6x plus 8 equals 0, trial and error factoring is slow. How do we solve quadratics directly?</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Invoke Pūraṇāpūraṇābhyām — By Completion or Non-Completion! Move the constant to the right: x² + 6x = -8. Now complete the imperfect square on the left into a perfect square!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak><prosody rate='90%'>Invoke Puranapuranabhyam — By Completion or Non-Completion! Move constant 8 to the right: x squared plus 6x equals minus 8. Now complete the imperfect square on the left into a perfect square!</prosody></speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: To complete x² + 6x, take half of the x-coefficient: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, and square it: 3² = 9! Add 9 to both sides: x² + 6x + 9 = -8 + 9 ⟹ (x + 3)² = 1! Taking square roots yields x + 3 = ±1, giving roots x = -2 or x = -4!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Take half of 6, which is 3, and square it: 3 squared is 9! Adding 9 to both sides yields x plus 3 squared equals 1, giving roots minus 2 and minus 4!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Now test your understanding, Shishya! In x² + 6x = -8, what completion term must you add to both sides to complete (x + 3)²? Calculate (6 ÷ 2)²!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Now test your understanding, Shishya! To complete the square for x squared plus 6x, calculate 6 divided by 2 quantity squared!</speak>

interactive_handshake.prompt_text: Calculate (6 / 2)² to find the completion term.

english_meaning: Specific and General / Part and Whole

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Factoring biquadratic expressions like x⁴ - 10x² + 9 feels overwhelming.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Factoring biquadratics like x to the fourth minus 10x squared plus 9 feels overwhelming.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Break the whole into parts! Let u = x². The equation reduces to u² - 10u + 9 = (u - 1)(u - 9)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Break the whole into parts! Substitute u equals x squared to factor easily!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: The roots are ±1 and ±3 without any cubic or quartic formulas!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>The roots are plus-or-minus 1 and plus-or-minus 3!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Tap the positive root corresponding to x² = 9!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Tap the positive root corresponding to x squared equals 9!</speak>

english_meaning: The Remainders by the Last Digit

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Converting fractions like 1/7 into exact repeating decimals takes forever by long division.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Converting fractions like 1 over 7 into repeating decimals takes forever.</speak>
<speak>Track the remainders! Each remainder generates the next decimal digit immediately!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: The digits 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7 form the cyclic pattern instantly!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>The digits form the cyclic pattern 142857 instantly!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: What is the remainder when 10 is divided by 7? Tap the remainder!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>What is the remainder when 10 is divided by 7? Tap the remainder!</speak>

english_meaning: The Ultimate and Twice the Penultimate

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Rational equations like 1/(x+2) + 1/(x+3) = 1/(x+1) + 1/(x+4) take messy cross-multiplications.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Rational equations like this take messy cross-multiplications.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Penultimate sum is (2+3)=5, Ultimate sum is (1+4)=5. When equal, set the numerator sum to 0: 2x + 5 = 0!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Penultimate and ultimate sums match! Simply set 2x plus 5 equals 0!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 2x = -5 gives x = -2.5 without expanding quadratic denominators!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>2x equals minus 5 gives x equals minus 2.5 in one step!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: For 2x + 6 = 0, tap the magnitude of x (|-3| = 3)!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>For 2x plus 6 equals 0, tap the magnitude of x!</speak>

english_meaning: The Product of the Sum is the Sum of the Products

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: How do I verify if (x + 2)(x + 3) = x² + 5x + 6 without recalculating every term?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>How do I verify polynomial factor expansions without recalculating every term?</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Set x = 1! Factor sum product: (1+2)(1+3) = 3 × 4 = 12. Expansion sum: 1 + 5 + 6 = 12. They match!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Set x equals 1! Both the factor sum product and expansion sum equal 12!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 12 equals 12 proves the expansion is 100% accurate in one check!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>12 equals 12 proves the expansion is completely accurate!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: For (x + 1)(x + 2), what is the factor sum product at x = 1: (2 × 3)?

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>What is the factor sum product at x equals 1 for x plus 1 times x plus 2?</speak>

english_meaning: The Factors of the Sum is the Sum of the Factors

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Factorizing 2x² + 5x + 2 requires checking multiple product pairs.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Factorizing 2x squared plus 5x plus 2 requires checking multiple product pairs.</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Evaluate Sc(expression): 2 + 5 + 2 = 9. Sc(factors) must multiply to 9: (2(1)+1)(1+2) = 3 × 3 = 9!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Expression coefficient sum is 9. Factor sums multiply to 3 times 3 equals 9!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: (2x + 1)(x + 2) is verified as the true factor pair!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>2x plus 1 times x plus 2 is verified as the true factor pair!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: You have mastered all 16 Vedic Sutras, Shishya! Tap 9 to begin your grand master trial!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>You have mastered all 16 Vedic Sutras, Shishya! Tap 9 to begin your trial!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: Finding the vertex turning point of 2x² - 8x + 5 usually takes full derivative formulas!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Finding the vertex turning point of quadratics usually takes full formulas!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Apply Calana-Kalanābhyām! Differentiate mentally: 2(2x) - 8 = 0 $\implies$ 4x = 8.

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Apply the differential sutra! 4x minus 8 equals 0!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: SHISHYA
dialogue_nodes.text: 4x = 8 $\implies$ x = 2! That gives the critical point in two seconds!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>4x equals 8, so x is 2! That gives the critical point in two seconds!</speak>

dialogue_nodes.speaker: GURU
dialogue_nodes.text: Solve for the turning point x: 4x = 8. Tap the root!

audio_cues.ssml_text: <speak>Solve for the turning point x: 4x equals 8. Tap the root!</speak>
